module purpose: neorv32_debug_dtm synchronizes the JTAG TCK/TMS/TDI inputs into clk_i, runs a scan-controller state machine, captures and shifts instruction/data registers, and serializes the selected bit on jtag_tdo_o. It also turns updates of the DMI scan register into dmi_req_o requests, latches dmi_rsp_i data and acknowledgment, and returns status/data through the JTAG scan path.

use-case flows.value: synchronized JTAG samples and derived TCK edge events used by the local scan logic
scan-controller phase sequencing and DR-update pulse generation
selected instruction/data-register contents shifted to jtag_tdo_o
DTM reset-control state captured from the DTMCS register and reflected into DTMCS readback
accepted DMI command fields captured from the DMI register and driven on dmi_req_o
returned DMI data and sticky error status packed for later JTAG readback
asynchronous clearing of synchronized JTAG samples, scan state/registers, TDO, and DMI controller state; plus clearing of err by DMI reset controls

conceptual assets.reasoning: The phase register advances only on synchronized TCK rising events and sampled TMS (lines 121-139), and that stored phase gates the DR-update pulse (lines 151-156), instruction/data capture and shifting (lines 178-197), and TDO selection (lines 203-210). Corrupting this state makes the implemented scan sequencing incorrect; availability is also established because transitions occur whenever rstn_i='1' and the sampled edge condition occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Current instruction register value selecting the active scan register
conceptual assets.reasoning: The instruction register is forced to the IDCODE address in reset/capture and shifted from the sampled serial input in IR_SHIFT (lines 178-181). Its value then selects which data register is captured or shifted (lines 186-197), what jtag_tdo_o returns (lines 204-210), and whether DTMCS or DMI updates affect the DMI controller (lines 247, 258, 265). Integrity of this stored decision is therefore required; availability is also established by serial readout in IR_SHIFT (line 204).

conceptual assets.concept: Identification code value reported on the IDCODE scan register
conceptual assets.reasoning: When DR_CAPTURE occurs with the instruction selecting the IDCODE register, the module loads `IDCODE_VERSION & IDCODE_PARTID & IDCODE_MANID & '1'` into tap_reg.idcode (line 187), shifts it in DR_SHIFT (line 194), and outputs it on jtag_tdo_o when that register is selected (line 207). The RTL therefore establishes integrity of the reported identification value, and availability when the IDCODE path is captured and shifted.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI reset-control state carried by DTMCS and used by the DMI controller
conceptual assets.reasoning: The DTMCS scan register is held locally and read on a valid DR update: `dmi_ctrl.dmireset <= tap_reg.dtmcs(16)` and `dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset <= tap_reg.dtmcs(17)` (lines 247-249). Those stored control bits are cleared when idle (lines 250-252), clear the sticky error flag when asserted (lines 256-257), and dmihardreset blocks new DMI command acceptance (line 265). Their current state is also reflected back into DTMCS readback through lines 220-221 and serialized through line 208. Integrity and conditional availability of this control state are therefore established.

conceptual assets.concept: Accepted DMI request command fields: address, write data, and operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: When no request is active and hard reset is not asserted, a valid DR update with the DMI register selected causes the controller to capture `tap_reg.dmi(40 downto 34)` into dmi_ctrl.addr and `tap_reg.dmi(33 downto 02)` into dmi_ctrl.wdata; if the low bits request read or write, dmi_ctrl.op is loaded and busy is asserted (lines 265-270). The captured fields are then delivered on the module boundary by lines 283-285. By the boundary-integrity rule, the consumer must receive exactly these values; availability is established under the RTL-visible acceptance conditions at lines 264-270.

The controller marks a request in progress by setting dmi_ctrl.busy when an accepted DMI command carries a read or write opcode (line 270), uses that state to block new command loading and to choose response handling (lines 264-276), raises the sticky error flag on an overlapping DMI update while busy (lines 258-259), and clears busy only when `dmi_rsp_i.ack = '1'` (lines 275-276). Integrity of this stored decision is required for correct request serialization and completion handling; availability is established because the state is cleared by the explicit acknowledgment condition.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI result and sticky error status returned through the DMI scan register
conceptual assets.reasoning: While a request is active, the controller latches returned data from `dmi_rsp_i.data` into dmi_ctrl.rdata (line 274). The sticky error flag is cleared by the reset controls (line 257) and set on an overlapping DMI update while busy (line 259). The value reported back to JTAG is then assembled as `dmi_ctrl.addr & dmi_ctrl.rdata & replicate_f(dmi_ctrl.err, 2)` (line 229), captured into tap_reg.dmi on DR_CAPTURE (line 189), and shifted out on jtag_tdo_o when the DMI register is selected (line 209); the same error status is also mirrored into DTMCS by line 224. Integrity is therefore established for the returned result/status payload, with availability under the response-latch and capture/shift conditions visible in the RTL.
